cohort: 60,502 pregnant women (597 twin pregnancies and 59,005 singleton pregnancies) receiving care at refugee and migrant clinics on the Thai Myanmar border
finding: Twin pregnancies in this setting were associated with higher maternal morbidity (especially pre-eclampsia, gestational hypertension, and eclampsia) and perinatal mortality, particularly for the second twin, compared to singleton pregnancies.
mod_finding: While three-quarters of twin pregnancies resulted in vaginal births, the study does not directly compare mode of delivery outcomes.
